messages:
jonah: heads-up — since 10:12 UTC we're seeing a spike of 429s from the rerank capacity lane in us-east. high queue lengths on egress, tail latency up.
infra-bot: ALERT: rerank-lane-us-east | 429-rate 6.2% over 5m | avg-queue-depth 38 | nodes@90% cpu
mia: can you paste a sample request_id and a small log snippet?
jonah: req=rx-4a7c3f; log snippet: `egress_queue_wait_ms=312; lane=rerank; gpu_mem_util=0.72; admission_drop=true`
arpit: checking autoscaler + pod evictions now. any recent config changes to max_inflight_per_lane or egress_weight?
jonah: not from our side. last change was 2 days ago (softlimit bump), but traffic pattern changed with a customer performing a large rerank job.
kevin: quick mitigation idea: temporarily lower rerank simultaneous_inflight to 6 and enable fallback routing to the embed lane for non-critical reranks. buys headroom.
sara: agree. fallback to embed-lite for > 2s queue waiters. we should also emit a throttle-signal metric so observability can track soft-drops.
mia: plan: 1) push routing tweak to route ~20% of low-priority rerank to embed-lite 2) reduce max_inflight for rerank lane 3) open an incident page. I'll run the change unless anyone objects.
arpit: +1, but watch for increased token-cost on embed-lite — it will be slightly cheaper per-token but may increase effective latency for those requests.
kevin: cost note: if this becomes frequent we should provision a small dedicated rerank burst pool (mixed GPU types) instead of continuous routing. one-off cost increase vs long-term savings from fewer fallbacks.
jonah: executing step 1 now — applying routing policy: `{
  "route": "rerank",
  "fallback": "embed-lite",
  "fallback_percent": 20,
  "priority_threshold": "low"
}`
deploy-bot: runbook: apply-routing-policy job started by mia at 10:25 UTC
mia: applied. lowering max_inflight_per_lane on rerank to 6. monitoring.
infra-bot: NOTIFY: rerank-lane-us-east config-change detected by policy-service
arpit: metrics: 429-rate fell to 3.1% in 4m, avg-queue-depth -> 21. latency p95 still elevated, but tail improving.
kevin: good. can we enable an admission_backpressure metric and an alert on oscillation so we don't thrash autoscaler?
sara: yes, add hysteresis: require 2 consecutive 5m windows before scaling up rerank pool. also add a budget check to avoid unbounded costs.
jonah: confirming monitoring graphs look better. will keep the 20% fallback for 1h then review.
mia: opened incident doc and assigned postmortem to infra/egress team. tag me if you want edits.
deploy-bot: policy-service: routing-policy applied successfully at 10:28 UTC
arpit: follow-up: we should explore a small pre-warmed rerank lane with shorter init times rather than fallback routing — less jitter for SLAs.
kevin: agree, but we need a cost model. i'll sketch options: on-demand burst vs pre-reserved vs preemptible fallback.
sara: ok. action items: 1) postmortem in 24h 2) cost model from kevin 3) prototype pre-warmed burst pool (eng-infra) 4) add throttle-signal metric (obs team)
jonah: thanks all. keep watching, will update if it resurges.
infra-bot: RESOLVED? rerank-lane-us-east 429-rate back below 1% at 10:41 UTC (was 6.2% at alert)
mia: closing incident page draft, leaving mitigation notes for postmortem. :thumbsup:
